mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% is accompanied by a decline in HOUST (industrial production), signaling labor market weakness that depresses equity valuations and drives negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 5% while HOUST falls in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite UNRATE > 5% and HOUST declines (p-value < 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) of at least 3% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained demand for equities.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05) when GDPC1 increases by <3% in a month or over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% in a month coincides with a positive 5-day forward return as market anticipates supply-side shocks reducing competition and raising valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when INDPRO declines by <5% in the prior month (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive 20-day forward returns as lower borrowing costs boost equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months and not in recession regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the FEDFUNDS threshold is breached or recession is detected (per NBER macro variables).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment) by 10,000 or more in a month coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates labor market weakness and slower growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >10,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS decline is <10,000 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both GDPC1 and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% in the same month suggest resilient demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase by <2% (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of 0.3% or more for two months suggests inflation stickiness, which predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL increases by less than 0.3% over two months (p > 0.05).
